TRAVEL NURSE CONTRACT COMPARISON CALCULATOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Which travel nurse offer actually pays more?

Enter up to three offers. See take-home per week and per year after tax, health premium, housing, travel and the unpaid weeks between contracts, what happens if the hospital cancels shifts, and the taxable hourly rate a weaker offer would need to match the best one.

Nothing you type leaves this browser tab. Illustrative estimates, not advice. Not legal, tax, or financial advice.

1. Your tax picture

Social Security and Medicare (7.65%) are added on top of the rate you enter, for taxable pay only. This is one flat percentage, not a tax return. Whether you have a tax home is a tax question this tool cannot answer.

2. The offers

Leave Offer C's taxable rate empty to compare two. Housing and travel cost are what you pay at the assignment beyond what you would pay at home anyway, for example rent on a second place. For a staff job near home, enter 0. Your rent at home is not modelled, so duplicate-expense costs of keeping a tax home are on you to consider.

How it works, and what it leaves out

  • Taxable pay: (rate x guaranteed hours + rate x overtime multiplier x overtime hours) x share of shifts actually paid. Tax is your rate plus 7.65% on that.
  • Stipends and travel reimbursement: untaxed if you say you keep a tax home, otherwise taxed like wages. If you enter a per-diem rate, stipends above 7 x that daily rate are flagged.
  • Bonus: always taxed. Costs: health premium and housing per week, travel once. Gap: unpaid weeks add to the period the take-home is averaged over.
  • Not modelled: tax brackets, state residency, the actual per-diem table, retirement matches, licence and compact fees, agency deductions, benefits beyond the premium, duplicate-expense rules and the audit risk of stipends.
  • Unverified: the arithmetic is checked by hand calculation only, not against a real payroll stub. If yours disagrees, that is the priority report.

Common questions

What is the real take-home of a travel nurse contract?

Not the weekly gross in the recruiter's text. It is taxable wages after tax, plus stipends if they really are untaxed, minus your health premium, the housing and travel you pay for, and averaged over the unpaid weeks between assignments. This tool does that arithmetic for up to three offers side by side.

Why can a higher weekly gross pay less?

Stipend-heavy packages look big but depend on hours being guaranteed and on you keeping a qualifying tax home. A lower gross with a higher taxable rate can be worth more once overtime, cancelled shifts and the weeks between contracts are counted.

What is a tax home?

In general, a regular place of business or post of duty, or a home you keep and pay for where you actually live and work part of the time. If you do not have one, agencies generally must treat stipends as taxable wages. This tool only asks you to say whether you do; it cannot decide for you. Ask a tax professional.

What is a guaranteed hours clause?

A promise that you are paid for the scheduled hours even if the hospital cancels your shifts. Without it, low-census cancellations reduce pay, and some agencies also reduce the stipends in proportion. The sensitivity table shows what 10, 20 and 30 percent cancelled shifts do to each offer.

How is overtime paid?

Usually at 1.5 times the taxable hourly rate, not the total package rate. A stipend-heavy offer with a low taxable rate therefore pays much less for extra shifts. Enter the multiplier your contract states.

What does this tool leave out?

Actual tax brackets, state residency rules, the exact per-diem rate for each city and date, retirement matches, licensure and compact fees, agency-specific deductions, referral bonuses and the value of benefits beyond the premium you type. The tax rate is a single percentage you choose.

Is my information uploaded anywhere?

No. Everything you type stays in this browser tab. There are no accounts, cookies or analytics vendors.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a tax professional, your agency or your employer. Results are illustrative estimates that depend entirely on the values you enter. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it and before signing a contract.

Independent. Not affiliated with any staffing agency, hospital or government agency. Tax descriptions identify the general idea and are not a legal opinion.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your rates and offers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (contracts_compared, example_loaded, report_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Own a place travel nurses rent? The mid-term rental calculator weighs a furnished 30-day-plus rental against a long-term lease and nightly renting.

Working extra shifts? The overtime pay calculator shows what a week with overtime pays.

Weighing a permanent employed physician or APP offer instead? The physician wRVU compensation calculator compares base, productivity and fixed-salary pay.

Employed physician comparing a base-plus-wRVU offer? The physician wRVU contract calculator shows the effective rate per wRVU and the crossover between two offers — nothing uploaded. Locum tenens clinician on a 1099? The locum tenens vs employed calculator compares that contract with a W-2 offer.

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.
